scientific_hypothesis: Compressing layers 1-3 to 40-60 nm and expanding layers 5-8 to 100-140 nm will sharpen the spectral roll-off between UV reflection (200-400 nm) and SWIR transmission (800-1500 nm) bands, improving dual-band separation compared to uniform 100 nm initialization.
expected_advantages: Sharper spectral transition between UV rejection and SWIR transmission bands
Reduced optimizer oscillation due to 20% step size reduction
Better exploitation of iteration_05 configuration knowledge
known_risks: Overly narrow seed ranges may trap optimizer in local minimum
Layer 4 boundary effects between compressed and expanded regions may create unintended interference
expected_observations: If hypothesis holds, best_target_score should rise across rounds as thickness optimization decouples the two bands, and tightest_margin should not fall
Aperiodic design should show lower reflectance in 800-1500 nm compared to Route 1's periodic stack
UV reflectance 200-400 nm should match or exceed Route 1 with fewer layers (24 vs 28)
If hypothesis fails, best_target_score will not exceed Route 1's score and valid_candidates will decrease as thickness combinations become physically invalid
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If valid_candidates falls below 5 for three consecutive rounds, expand the thickness bounds to 20-250 nm and continue
If tightest_margin remains below 0.05 for four consecutive rounds, fix the 6 thinnest layers and optimize only the remaining 18
